fields.v: Garg, N., Mohindra, R., Maru, S. (2026). Specifications as Governance Artifacts: Human-AI Collaboration and Oversight for AI-Generated Code. In 2026 IEEE Conference on Generative AI for Secure Systems (GAISS), 28-30 October 2026, University of Texas at Austin. IEEE. DOI: 10.1109/GAISS66401.2026.11779695 (6 pages)
Conference — IEEE Conference on Generative AI for Secure Systems (GAISS 2026), Austin, 28-30 October 2026; 6 pages
Independent researchers (Bothell, Redmond, Bentonville, United States; personal gmail addresses); no institutional affiliation

Proposes an approach; secondary: Evaluates — specification-driven governance framework (spec review gate, explicit baseline, drift detection, human reconciliation, RACI, audit trail, standards mapping); evaluated by a within-subject human study of baseline-anchored vs code-only drift review, an automated-reviewer replication, a supporting case study and controlled model studies

Specification-driven governance framework (authors' own, unnamed), version Not stated. In the model studies: 'one-shot' spec-then-code, 'staged' spec then fresh-generation implementation, spec-first prompting, chain-of-thought and direct generation arms

Specification, high-level design (HLD) and low-level design (LLD), approved together as the auditable baseline (invariants/clauses); RACI responsibility matrix (Table I); audit trail: approved baseline with approver and timestamp, drift log (each divergence and violated invariant/clause), reconciliation record (code or document changed, by whom, why)

Five control points: (1) spec authoring (spec, HLD, LLD before code); (2) specification review gate (approve as baseline); (3) guided generation (model generates code from approved documents); (4) drift detection (code vs baseline); (5) reconciliation (human resolves each drift by correcting code or updating documents and re-approving the baseline)

Specification review gate modelled on HLD/LLD reviews (criteria: completeness, clear interfaces, explicit constraints, testable behaviour); drift review against the baseline; human reconciliation of every flagged drift; accountability always with a named human (Owner accountable, Table I)

Human and automated-reviewer studies: drift review step only (reviewing AI-generated code against an approved spec/HLD/LLD vs code only). Case study: full workflow (author walkthrough). Model studies: spec delivery modes (specification as separate artefact vs prompt text)

Not stated in Böckeler's terms; cites Piskala's spec-first to spec-as-source levels; framework treats the approved specification as source of truth and baseline kept in sync by reconciliation (closest to spec-anchored, classification by the drafter); long-term source-of-truth use is future work
New code generated from specifications (synthetic AI-generated banking services reviewed; insurance premium payment microservice in the case study; single-function families in model studies)

Human study: 2 services; Service A 1,040-line multi-file build with 11 verified drifts, Service B smaller with 10 verified drifts. Model studies: banking service with 20 invariants; 10 single-function families; 'three task scales'
Banking services (human and model studies); insurance premium payment microservice (case study)
Five reviewers with 3-10 years of experience (human study); case study by one author
Review time per review in minutes (human study)
Drift-review recall against adjudicated ground truth (verified drifts); model studies: pass rate on held-out invariants scored by an executable checker; failed-to-assemble builds
None
Review time (≈48 vs 27 min); mean drifts found; reviewer confidence (1-5); inter-reviewer agreement (Fleiss' kappa)
Attribution rate: share of findings tied to a specific named requirement/invariant (traceability/accountability)

Manual: reviewers record each drift, violated rule, location, start/end time and confidence; ground truth by adjudicating every distinct reviewer claim against the source code; paired Wilcoxon (human), Mann-Whitney (machine). Automatic: executable checker for model studies (validated with known correct and naive references)

Human study (criterion: adjudicated ground-truth drifts): (a) baseline-anchored review (spec+HLD+LLD) + human reviewers, n=5: recall 0.525, attribution 0.81, 5.6 drifts, 48.4 min, confidence 4.2. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors. (b) code-only review + human reviewers (comparison condition): recall 0.518, attribution 0.00, 5.4 drifts, 26.7 min, confidence 3.4. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors. Automated-reviewer replication, 90 reviews by Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro (agent Not stated; per-model values Not stated): (c) baseline-anchored: recall 0.376, attribution 0.67. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. (d) code-only: recall 0.377, attribution 0.00. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. Model studies (models and agent Not stated): (e) staged spec then fresh generation + weak model: pass rate 45.0% (n.s., n=4), failed builds -50%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. (f) one-shot spec+code + weak model: 23.8%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. (g) direct generation + weak model (baseline): 23.8%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. (h) spec-first + two strong assistants: e.g. 92%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. (i) chain-of-thought + two strong assistants: e.g. 95%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. (j) direct + two strong assistants (baseline): e.g. 59%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: not measured. Case study: framework caught 2 issues at the review gate and 2 by drift detection; unconstrained run kept both defects (illustrative, author-conducted; no verdict)

Human study: within-subject, counterbalanced 2x2 (condition x service); 5 reviewers each did one review per condition; both services reviewed in each condition; no code execution, AI tools or web; baseline condition = code-only (public API only). Held constant: services, ground truth, attribution definition. Acceptance criterion: adjudicated ground truth (11 + 10 verified drifts), not the test suite. Repetitions: one review per reviewer per condition. Automated replication: same 2x2 design with 3 models, 90 reviews. Model studies: held-out scored criteria withheld from prompts; arms one-shot vs staged vs direct (n=4) and CoT vs spec-first vs direct over 10 function families and 2 assistants

Baseline-anchored vs code-only (human): recall 0.525 vs 0.518 (p=0.69, n.s.); attribution 0.81 vs 0.00 (p=0.043); time 48.4 vs 26.7 min (p=0.043); confidence 4.2 vs 3.4 (p=0.068); Fleiss' kappa 0.20-0.63. Machine: recall 0.376 vs 0.377 (p=0.95); attribution 0.67 vs 0.00 (p<10^-4), consistent across models. Model studies: staged 45.0% vs direct/one-shot 23.8% (p≈0.18, n=4, n.s.); spec-first vs CoT not significant (p≈0.28-0.32), CoT captures almost all spec-first gain

Distinguished conditions on attribution and time, not on recall. Repeatable: pattern reproduced by the automated replication. Limitations stated: n=5, signed-rank test floor p=0.043; confidence subjective; agreement on small groups; ground truth by adjudication because a test suite missed real drift; attribution measures traceability, not fix correctness; machine replication is convergent, not confirmatory; case study author-conducted; staged result has second-pass confound; model strength a dominant confound

Human study intentionally small (5 reviewers, 2 services, one domain); effects significant only for tested tasks; results 'preliminary and directional', 'strong pilot finding'. Framework adds upfront review cost; less value for short-lived or low-risk work; deployment difficulties: authoring discipline and spec-code synchronisation. Future work: spec as long-term source of truth after check-in, automated drift detection against LLD data contracts and state machines, LLM pre-screen (untested), larger human study with more reviewers, tasks and mid-strength models
